items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had regular visits from Hunerto and would give him enough to make a few sticks every time he came.

ctx.x: It taken me a whole afternoon to do that, and when it was finished, I had a mountain of gage. I had bought a pair of shoes not long before this and still had the box, so I filled that and still had more. I filled another box about half the size of the shoe box and put some in a newspaper package. Then I became scared and started to wonder if Pépé had brought me all that stuff to get me in trouble with the law. I wondered where I could hide the stuff and the only place I could see in the room was the top of a…

was the ideal place to conceal the stuff for a special reason. I said before that this hotel was a second rate one, although my room was nice for that type of hotel. The bed was clean and sheets were changed every week. The maid cleaned everywhre except under the bed and on top of the cabinets, so when I looked on top of the one in my room, there was dust thick enough to plant potatoes. I took my boxes and the package, put them on top of the cabinet and covered them with dust. Then I breathed a sigh of relief and…

The Edouard's band, Don Byas and myself were still doing concerts and in April, we went to Knokke for three days at the casino with a big show. This was the 16th, 17th and 18th. The show included the orchestras of Bernard Hilda and Maurice Toubas. They were both known as high society orchestras in Europe, and we took care of the jazz department.
